attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter. The quoted 'fastest growing' phrase is framing, but the causal assertion is his.

semantics.note: A firm causal claim: growth came from media hype, not usefulness. The normalisation keeps the 'can't explain' clause, and the contract rightly treats that clause as rhetorical.

contract.note: The plain reading, that usefulness played essentially no part, is the ordinary meaning of 'didn't grow because it was useful... but because'. Using growing task-based use and reported helpfulness as the test is fair and not stretched.

evidence.note: Independent Pew survey (Feb–Mar 2025): ChatGPT use for work rose to 28% and use for learning to 26%, both growing since 2023. Concrete task use grew within the period.
Pew survey (Oct 2024): 40% of workers who use chatbots for work call them highly helpful for speed. Covers chatbots generally, not ChatGPT alone, but it is within the period.
66% of US adults had not used ChatGPT. This bears on 'everybody would try it', not on the cause of growth.
OpenAI's own study, covering data past the period. A company disclosure, so context only.

reviews.rationale: Independent Pew data from the period shows growing use of ChatGPT for work and learning, and a substantial share of users finding chatbots highly helpful. That meets the contract's contradiction condition. Hype may have driven trial, but the claim rules out any role for usefulness, and the evidence shows usefulness contributed. The surveys cannot fully separate the two causes, but the claim's absolute exclusion does not survive.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion about CoreWeave in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Will crush the life out of the company' is unhedged, so this is a scored forecast. October is fairly read as October 2025, the next October after the May 2025 post.

contract.note: Reading 'crush the life out of' as default, distressed restructuring, or inability to operate is an ordinary reading of the metaphor. The deadline choice is flagged and reasonable.

evidence.note: The FY2025 10-K shows 43 data centers operating and strong growth at year-end 2025. That weighs against collapse, but the quoted text does not reconcile the October obligations or show they were paid.
Verge, Nov 2025: an analyst says CoreWeave borrows to pay interest, and an earlier waived technical default is noted. Neither is tied to October payments or shows severe distress.

reviews.rationale: The October 2025 deadline has passed. No evidence shows default or distressed restructuring caused by October payments, so the support condition is not met. Continued operations at year-end 2025 weigh against the forecast. But the packet has no record showing the October obligations were met or refinanced, which the contract's contradiction condition requires, and the packet's own stated gaps admit this. The evidence does not settle the outcome.

attribution.note: Zitron's own characterisation of the 'middle manager brain'.

semantics.note: The sentence describes the disposition of a managerial archetype, not a dated prediction. Even as a conditional forecast, the antecedent is undefined and its status unknown, so it would not be scored.

contract.note: The contract correctly finds no population, threshold, or observable test. Declining to score is fair to the speaker's words.

evidence.note: A 2025 survey of managers' attitudes toward replacing staff with AI. It does not match qualifying replacement opportunities to actual dismissals.

reviews.rationale: This generic characterisation of a managerial archetype has no defined population, frequency, horizon, or observable meaning of 'won't hesitate'. If read as a conditional, the antecedent's status is unknown. It cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. The quoted phrases are reasons he attributes to reporters, not claims he endorses.

semantics.note: The normalisation leaves out the stated reasons ('because' inference costs are falling and the companies have smart people) and adds 'only'. The core assertion about reporters' refusal and motives is mostly kept.

contract.note: The contract fairly finds that the main assertion, about reporters' refusal and its motives, is unbounded and unobservable. It rightly declines to score on the loose free-to-play comparison, which cuts against his own point if read literally.

evidence.note: CNBC, 2024: OpenAI expected about a $5B loss on $3.7B revenue. Supports only the subordinate 'burn billions' clause.
A weak secondary source puts 2024 free-to-play revenue near $118B. Background for the loose benchmark only.

reviews.rationale: The central claim, that reporters as a group refuse to speak bluntly for stated reasons, has no defined scope or observable test. The money clauses are subordinate. 'Burn billions' holds for OpenAI, but scoring the sentence on that aside would not test what he asserted.
